en: We've met?
How dare ye forget the face o'the local merrymaker and agitator.
You've drank my booze, Returner! Well, t'weren't mine, but presentation is what matters.
When... Did that happen?
Few weeks ago, no more! Do Vultures have a short memory? On account of all that mindless wanderin'?
Wouldn't drink anything you offered.
Gods! I see those nasty Bandits shot a hole through your heart!
You'll sing a different tune when the bonfires are lit once again!
Spoils to spare...?
If you may, only if you may. Y'see, words have power, Returner... Some are much too dreadful...
You will never hear me say handout... But donation, that is a beautiful term.
What's that about a gathering?
Y'see, the next social gathering I have planned will be momentous. Folks from the Rada, maybe even Gunners!, will come together for this one.
We need fuel, fuel for the pyres in our souls! Contributions are much appreciated.
Tell me more about these parties.
Of course, sir!
Wanna ask about folks around here...
Oh, people are my whole deal! Ask away.
Tell me a story.
Sorry, but I need more time to workshop the material! It's an art, after all – it takes time...
Got to go.
How do these gatherings usually go?
We join around a fire, like all men throughout History – from the cavemen to the Westernites. We drink and sing, play the ol' guitar and tell stories.
Marko's good for a song and a tale, if nothing else! Chords from my homeland, melodies of my own creation... Legends and myths and trivial goings-on, embellished by my lyricism!
And there is booze, and also drink, plus a lot of alcohol!
Booze, alcohol and drink...?
Everything's better in threes, man! That's not just a rule for jokes, but the mythical structure of mankind's many stories!
Sounds good.
It does, doesn't it? Well if it does, then please – contribute to the cause!
Donations?
Yes, well, apologies for all the asking and no giving. The last "gathering" was very lively and folks felt the freedom to... Take from my personal stash while I was inebriated.
'Twas cowardly, but Marko understands the temptation. Now, alas, I'm hung out to dry – much like a recently-shot Vulture, I s'pose!
Who usually goes to these events?
The salt of the earth! Brown-nosed folks like you and I, who hang their dirty heads down as they walk, afraid of power structures we cannot escape!...
O, to be a nobleman from bygone times!
Shouldn't you spend on more important things?
Hmmm. More important than art and joy? What would those things be?
About something else.
I've talked enough.
Survival.
I survive just fine on the kindness of others. I entertain, Returner; everyone loves an entertainer.
Besides, man hungers for more than food, thirsts for more than water! What is survival without living? Nay, these celebrations are much too important.
Weaponry.

Ha! These hands are made for love and song, not for brutal violence. All men are equal despite different inclinations, which we should strive to enable. Don't oppress me with your gritty worldview, man!
Something that'll actually help Zalesye.
What are you saying?! Philistine! These gatherings are the pulsing blood, the drum-beating heart of Zalesye!

Look around you – life is full of dread! God knows we need the entertainment; 'tis downright noble to sing and dance through stormy weather. Heck, even sticks-in-the-butt like the Rada can get down when properly inspired!
You know what – never mind.
Alright, I guess.
You like the folks that come to gather?
There's beauty in every soul, my friend! Palatines are fun to lock arms with when they're not starting fights. Rada are a bit preachy, of course, but it's funny how they can't hold their drink.

Vultures... Don't approach us very often. But when they do, they're nice enough to everybody! And Acolytes... Well, they don't come because they "disapprove". Which I don't understand. Were God down here with us, he'd be a heavy drinker with a mind for the arts!
You don't belong to any group?
Don't I? Why, I belong to the largest one of all – the Common Man! We outnumber all others fifteen to one! (Don't quote me on that.)
You Vultures are closer to us than any other, Returner. Keeping our heads down, wandering into subsistence... Relying always on communication before violence.
Doesn't all this drinking cause trouble?

Ahh, we do get rowdy! But what's a little fightin', a little rumble between brothers, compared to the dreads of this ragged wasteland? No, I'd say that most trouble brought by alcohol is no trouble at all!
The Hospital is not far off, in case anyone's nose needs fixin'!
Changing the subject...
See you later.
Hmmm, which one should I tell? Perhaps a new one I'm working on; help me workshop it, won't you, Returner? 'Tis the Lover's Tale:
"Not too long ago, a Rada man and an Acolyte lady were talking over a bonfire – an informal gathering, where the moon kindly shook away the Mist to illuminate and awe our two lovebirds...

They locked glistening eyes, chests pounding like war drums!, signals crossing like ships and lighthouses. They said without words: despite the mud, the violence, the dirt and hunger, the endless acidity of world-swallowing Mist – still, we needn't be alone.

It was a beautiful scene — the kind of beauty our uncultured hearts, in this apocalyptic land, are not built to withstand. The Rada man decided to get up and fetch the vodka he'd been hiding from the others.
Keep going...
...And then?
I'll hear the rest later. (Leave)
Uhm, wow, I see... Maybe this isn't a good one?...

A couple weeks he'd spent carefully stashing it under nondescript boxes in the corner of a shack – creeping in the night to enjoy his vice without risk. This wonderful secret would surely entice the lady, he thought, trying to steel his nerves.

She sat there contemplating the moon through the Mist; catching its light with her deep breaths. If only he knew no such thing as vodka was necessary! If only he'd embraced her then and there, ah! – it would have been a dream... But he went, and she waited, imagining what a warm embrace feels like.
He came back at last with the bottle, half-full and uncorked. He was shaking. She was so kind and beautiful, and him a brute!... This would be his only chance.
Hmmm...
I'll hear the rest later. (Leave)
Oh... Well, ok then...

She accepted a swig or two. He took a couple more. And as you know, dear listener, love and alcohol can reduce or amplify the senses: of time, of touch... Loving, drunken moments can either last forever or be cut short, abruptly reminding you of the rising sun, time's dry palms scraping your tired face...

This time, it was over in a blink. They spent the night in drunken bliss, but had not even a memory from it; their tender moments had flown past like a flock of scared birds, disappearing over a frozen lake as gunshots rung out beneath. It was already time to get to work. Time for mud, for violence, for Zalesye.

Well, the man from the Rada, rubbing his crusty eyes, started making his way back to camp as the Acolyte lady went to the Church. They were desolate. Their emotions seeped out from their pores like smoke from doused flames. Not sure what had even happened – no swelling on their lips, no trace of warmth on their cheeks – doubt and regret stabbed at them like the acid rains of the Dola.
Go on...
And then?
I'll catch the rest later, sorry. (Leave)
...I was getting to the good part...

The man arrived at camp and struggled to put these feelings to rest – much work to be done, after all. He grabbed a few tools and went to the main square, where he would make an announcement about the status of Rada-owned crops in the South, around Yarovit Park. Boring stuff.

He stepped on a tiny, improvised podium: tires stacked under a wooden plank. The Acolyte lady was still on his mind as he raised his arms to commence the speech and felt the cold wind blow through his alcohol-poisoned body. He noticed something strange: the wind's icy velvet enveloped him wholly – all of him, from top... To bottom.

His fellow members of the Rada, serious men and women, gathered for work and for the cause, all gasped in horrifying unison. They knew nothing of the sweet Acolyte lady, who sobbed quietly while dusting the far corners of a rundown Church... No, they knew only of the Rada man, distinguished, strict and severe, standing on a tiny box, armed of the right to speak and be heard; a respected leader...
But his words would never again be taken seriously, and that sight of him would forever be etched into their memories. For you see...
For you see, dear listener... As the man looked down, he realized in horror – in front of all those people!...
His penis was sticking out."
... *ahem*.
His <u>penis</u> was <u>sticking out.</u>
I heard.
Well. Yes, that's the story. A comedic tragedy. Seems I have to brush up on my delivery...
Anyway. That's it for today...
That's not a story, more like... A thing that happened.
Um... Well, yes. Seems I have to brush up on some storytelling fundamentals, huh? Music was always more my thing...
But that's it for today, I suppose.
Mr. Salt-of-the-earth himself! Remember ol' Marko? And more importantly: have ye spoils to spare?
Well met!
Hark! The man of the hour!
Afraid the party's over, any spoils for the next?
Marko – time for a chat?
Need to talk.
Let me ask you something.
Would like to trade.
Let's see about trading.
Wanna exchange goods.
I've not much to spare... Donations appreciated.
Can ye not spare a few items?
Don't have much to offer outside our gatherings...
'Fraid this will be a one-sided transaction...
Fare thee well!
I'll let you know when it's time to gather!
Aye, good luck out there!
Be seeing you later, then.

Ah! Glorious nectar! This makes a man loosen his lips. You see, the mixture that put me in that sorry state at Saint Anastasia gave me visions indeed: yet I remember them not, since I got blackout-drunk again right after leaving!
Aye, good luck out there!
Be seeing you later, then.

But I can tell you this: if you fancy a vision yourself, you may find that Mudlarks are quite good at producing the type of mixture that will get you there. I saw one of those providers not too far from here, somewhere around the place that was attacked and burned...
But now I'm good as new. What are you trying to do, threaten me?!

Have you gotten me my nectar yet, monsieur?
How about providing something in exchange? Like, say – a bottle of moonshine. A simple gesture 'fore I give ye the road to opening your third eye.
I don't share a connect that easily, sir. Nor do I trust a man I've not had a recent drink with. But I suppose that can be remedied.
I see! Well there's no need to rush. Unless you factor in my failing old mind, which forgets secrets before they're leaked.
